sections.name: Riot Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A riot-armoured infected found in The Parish and Cold Stream and in the Left 4 Dead 2 versions of No Mercy and Dead Air. Its front is immune to bullets and blows, so it can only be killed from behind, with fire, with explosions or with the chainsaw.
Weak points: Hit it from behind: shove it to stun it and step around it, or shove it off-centre so it spins and shows its back. Fire, explosions and the chainsaw still work from the front.
Looks like: An armoured guard in a helmet with a visor and a light blue (sometimes grey) uniform with a sheathed nightstick. The bands on its arm are reflective, so a flashlight picks them out.
Tips: Survivor bots cannot tell it from other infected and waste ammo shooting its front, and it is especially dangerous to an incapacitated player, who often cannot land a shot on its back from the floor. Avoid fighting it where it can crawl, because a crawling one cannot be shoved back.

sections.name: CEDA Worker Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A common infected in a hazmat suit that is immune to fire and may drop a bile bomb when killed. It has 150 health on Normal and above, and appears in Dead Center's Hotel and Streets, the lower floors of the hospital in No Mercy and Rayford's industrial area in The Sacrifice.
Weak points: Its suit makes it resistant to fire: a Molotov does not set it alight and incendiary ammo does not ignite it, though the bullets still hit, and one left idle in a fire for a long time dies from the heat. Shoot it in the head or hit it with a melee weapon.
Looks like: A hazmat suit with a visor, yellow or green (dark blue and white in the No Mercy hospital). The suit has reflective areas, and a bile bomb hangs at its side when it carries one.
Tips: If you have a free slot, pick up the bile bomb from its corpse and keep it for later. In the No Mercy hospital they are nearly the only source of bile bombs in the campaign, but they carry one quite rarely.

sections.name: Clown Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A fairground clown found in the Dark Carnival campaign. When it spots survivors it charges, and its squeaky shoes call the infected nearby to join the attack. It has 150 health on Normal and above.
Weak points: Any attack that hurts a common infected works on it. Shoving it honks its nose, and after four honks in a row the next shove kills it. If you kill one at a distance, the infected following it stop and mill about for a moment, so shoot them then.
Looks like: Oversized squeaky shoes and striped trousers (for example pink and blue, red and yellow, or blue and white), and a flower on its chest that sometimes squirts water.
Tips: A clown does not make the Director spawn more infected: it only stirs up the ones already nearby, and its pull has no effect during a horde attack. A tight group running from one direction behind a clown is easier to shoot than infected arriving from different directions.

sections.name: Mud Men
sections.card:
Summary: Infected covered in mud, found in the Swamp Fever campaign and also in the sewers of No Mercy and Death Toll and on The Last Stand's Junkyard map. They sprint on all fours, and a hit from one smears mud across your screen. They have 150 health on Normal and above.
Weak points: They have the same weaknesses as common infected but are slightly more resistant to damage, with 150 health on Normal and above (50 on Easy). They are faster because they move on all fours, so shoot them instead of trying to outrun them, and if the mud blurs your view, use a melee weapon.
Looks like: A common infected caked in reflective mud that moves low on all fours, though it stands on two legs when idle and stumbles back on two feet when shoved.
Tips: A pipe bomb thrown into the swamp pulls nearby mud men to it and kills them easily, and a bile bomb thrown in gathers them in one spot. Turning off gore in the game's settings also turns off the mud blinding.

sections.name: Worker Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A construction-crew infected with ear protection, a hard hat and a reflective vest, also called Road Crew. They fill the Hard Rain campaign and also appear in the Left 4 Dead 2 versions of No Mercy, Dead Air, The Sacrifice and The Last Stand. They have 150 health on Normal and above.
Weak points: They have the same weaknesses as common infected but are slightly more resistant to damage, with 150 health on Normal and above (50 on Easy). Their ear protection makes them unable to hear pipe bombs, so a thrown pipe bomb is useless unless it lands near them.
Looks like: Ear protectors, a yellow or white hard hat and a reflective vest, which is easiest to spot in the storms of Hard Rain.
Tips: A bile bomb that lands without hitting any infected does not draw them either: they go for the survivors instead, so aim it to hit several infected. They still react to car alarms and to a chainsaw, and they mostly react to movement they see, so you can sneak past one that is looking away.

sections.name: Fallen Survivor
sections.card:
Summary: A rare uncommon infected found in The Passing and, since the Last Stand update, also in the Left 4 Dead campaigns No Mercy, Death Toll, Crash Course and The Last Stand. It wears militia gear with a Molotov, pipe bomb, pills and first aid kit strapped on. It has 1000 health, cannot be set on fire and usually runs away when shot, and killing it can drop some of those items.
Weak points: A melee weapon kills it in one hit, and so do explosive ammo, the M60 and a headshot while it is still idle; a Magnum body shot does 500 damage. A shove briefly stops it running, but do not rely on shoves alone, because shove fatigue makes you wait three seconds.
Looks like: A man in militia clothes with a boonie cover and three ammo belts carrying a Molotov, pipe bomb, pills and first aid kit, in a blue, white or green shirt.
Tips: It can carry any of a Molotov, pipe bomb, pain pills and first aid kit, though sometimes only a single Molotov, and it drops them at random when killed. If it runs off it takes a long time to disappear, and the Director tends to generate another one sooner than usual.

sections.name: Molotov cocktail
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable weapon that sets a large area on fire for about 15 to 17 seconds. The fire spreads over time and burns every infected that touches it, and common infected that run into it burn to cinders.
Uses: Throw it at a choke point just as a horde reaches it, because infected do not try to avoid fire. On high difficulties keep one for a Tank, which cannot put itself out without water: a burning Tank survives on fire alone for 75 seconds on Easy and Normal, 80 on Advanced and 85 on Expert.
Tips: It only goes off when it hits the floor, not a wall or a special infected. Do not hit teammates: on Expert even a full-health survivor can die in the flames, and an incapacitated one inside the fire is hard to revive.

sections.name: Pipe bomb
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable bomb with a bright red light and a loudly beeping detector that draws common infected to it, then explodes 6 seconds after it is thrown. The blast is small, a little over three to four metres on Normal, but a well-placed bomb can kill 20 or more at once.
Uses: Use it to clear an open area of loosely gathered common infected, keep one for a big horde, or draw enemies away from a teammate who is incapacitated or covered in bile. Do not throw several: common infected run to the first and ignore the others.
Tips: In Left 4 Dead 2 it is less effective, because passive infected seem to respond more slowly to its beeping and smoke, and sometimes not at all. Throw it low to the ground, and shove away infected that are already close or they may ignore it. Special infected and worker infected are not drawn to it, and a Witch or Tank near the blast is stumbled but does not chase it.

sections.name: First aid kit
sections.card:
Summary: The healing item in the primary slot. It takes five seconds to use on yourself or a teammate, during which you cannot defend yourself, and it restores 80 percent of the missing health, so it never brings anyone back to full.
Uses: Used on a survivor in their final incapacitation state it heals them and resets their incapacitations. After an incapacitation a survivor has only 1 permanent health, so a kit then gives 80 health, and a kit also removes any extra health gained from pills.
Tips: Safe rooms and finales always have kits in their first aid cabinets, but on Expert kits are very rare during a level. Under adrenaline the heal takes three seconds instead of five. In Left 4 Dead 2 you can pick up a defibrillator or an ammo upgrade instead of a kit.

sections.name: Defibrillator
sections.card:
Summary: A one-use device, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that brings a dead survivor back to life. Select it to see the nearest corpse glow faintly red, walk up to it and hold the attack button for three seconds.
Uses: The revived survivor comes back with 50 permanent health and no items except the secondary weapon, so they must pick their dropped gear up from the ground. It works on any survivor corpse, even one whose owner has already been rescued from a closet.
Tips: You cannot carry a defibrillator and a first aid kit at the same time. They do not spawn often, usually one per level, and the Director tends to place one nearby when a survivor is on the verge of death. Someone who dies hanging from a ledge falls and cannot be revived.

sections.name: Pain pills and adrenaline shot
sections.card:
Summary: Two items for the temporary healing slot. Pain pills give 50 temporary health that slowly drains away, and the adrenaline shot, new in Left 4 Dead 2, gives 25 temporary health and a 15-second boost. Either can be handed to a teammate with the melee button.
Uses: Pills lose one point of temporary health every 3 seconds, so they last at most 150 seconds, and they also remove speed penalties when your total health is above 40. For 15 seconds adrenaline lets you run faster, shove without fatigue and use items, heal and revive faster, and the horde's slowing hits and water no longer slow you.
Tips: A first aid kit removes any extra health you gained from pills. While adrenaline lasts you get tunnel vision and mono sound, which makes it hard to tell where a sound came from.

sections.name: Grenade launcher
sections.card:
Summary: A single-shot primary weapon, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that fires a slow, looping grenade. The blast kills common infected and weaker special infected in a tight radius and stumbles the rest, except Chargers and Tanks. It holds one grenade with 30 in reserve, takes a long time to reload, and ammo piles cannot refill it.
Uses: A direct hit does 1000 damage to a Tank. It can also stumble a special infected that is pinning a teammate from a distance, and the pinned player takes no blast damage. Keep its shots for very large groups of infected or a horde.
Tips: Friendly fire is mild on lower difficulties but a real threat on higher ones, so switch to a secondary weapon in tight spaces or when a horde is right in front of you. Because the grenade explodes on contact, aim at a hard surface near the target, or from above at the middle of a horde, and lead moving targets because it flies slowly.

sections.name: M60 machine gun
sections.card:
Summary: A special-tier machine gun, new in Left 4 Dead 2, with a 150-round belt and no reloading. Ammo piles cannot refill it, and once the belt is empty it is dropped and you go back to your secondary weapon.
Uses: It kills a common infected in one shot wherever it hits, even on Expert Realism, and it never needs reloading. An ammo upgrade converts all the rounds left in the belt into incendiary or explosive rounds, so it makes the most of one.
Tips: Switch to your secondary weapon against small groups to save the belt for larger ones. Its accuracy matches the AK-47's, so it is poor at long range or on the move, and special ammo on a nearly empty M60 is wasted because it only converts what is left.

sections.name: Chainsaw
sections.card:
Summary: A special melee weapon for the sidearm slot, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that does 1000 damage per second and kills a common infected in one hit anywhere on the body. Its fuel cannot be refilled and once the gauge reads empty it is useless, but it burns no fuel while idle.
Uses: Special infected generally die in under half a second, the Charger in a little over, and a Tank takes 3, 4, 6 or 8 seconds on Easy, Normal, Advanced and Expert. It is the only melee weapon that cuts you free from a Smoker's tongue without precise aim or timing.
Tips: It needs a long rev-up, so start it before a horde reaches you, and being pinned or knocked down drops it back to idle. Its noise draws nearby common infected, and its arc hurts teammates, enough to incapacitate one on Realism, so keep your distance from them. Tap the fire button against small groups to save fuel.

sections.name: Incendiary and explosive ammo
sections.card:
Summary: Two ammo upgrades for any primary weapon in Left 4 Dead 2. They spawn at random, usually only a handful of times in a campaign, and take the first aid kit slot: you put the pile down on the ground, which takes several seconds, and each player can use it once to get one extra magazine of the special ammo.
Uses: Incendiary ammo sets common and special infected on fire, but not CEDA worker infected, Jimmy Gibbs Junior or the Fallen Survivor, and it kills a common infected in one hit. Explosive ammo explodes on any surface, instantly kills all common infected and stumbles any special infected except the Tank.
Tips: Explosive rounds hurt you and nearby teammates at point blank, which can be devastating on Advanced and Expert, and they can set off gas cans, propane tanks, fireworks and oxygen tanks. Using one type while the other is active replaces it, because they do not stack.
